description: On a small JavaScript library (node:test, eslint, kebab-case files, camelCase functions, a ValidationError class, *-test.js tests) that already has a standards/index.yml with two seeded rules and a CLAUDE.md with no standards pointer, a non-interactive discover-standards run merges into the existing index: version/generated/stack/standards keys, a stack that matches the fixture, well-formed rules (id category-NNN, rule under 80 characters, example under 60, at least 6 rules over 3 categories), the two seeded rules kept with new ids continuing after them, rules grounded in the codebase's real conventions, an expanded standards/<category>.md for any category over 3 rules, exactly one standards pointer appended to CLAUDE.md, and nothing written outside standards/ and CLAUDE.md. The checks cover structure and grounding, not whether the rules are good or complete. The fixture is a one-commit repository, so the git-commit-style rules cannot be checked against history. The skill and its command (/ensemble-core:ensemble:discover-standards) live in packages/core; the baseline arm has no plugin and is expected to measure what the plugin's conventions (index.yml format, merge-first, CLAUDE.md pointer) add to a plain 'extract our coding standards' request; the baseline gets the same prompt and no command. Uncertain until a trial: the command manifest is marked user-invocable: false and the skill disable-model-invocation: true, so whether the typed command runs in the with-skill arm is unproven.
prompt: Analyze this codebase and record its coding conventions as project standards in a standards/ directory with a machine-readable standards/index.yml. A standards/index.yml already exists: keep what it says and add to it, do not start over. Add a short pointer to the standards to CLAUDE.md if it has none. This is a non-interactive run: ask no questions and choose the recommended option for anything unclear. Write only under standards/ and to CLAUDE.md. Do not change source code, run the tests or install anything.
